business_problem: Verizon needed a data layer that could run at the network edge so 5G and IoT applications could avoid regional-cloud bottlenecks and keep data synchronized with minimal latency across mobile zones.
solution_summary: Verizon is working with MongoDB to create a reference architecture for data at the edge of its 5G network. The company extends AWS compute and storage into Verizon service-access points through AWS Wavelength, then overlays MongoDB Atlas and Realm so applications can keep operational data close to users instead of routing everything through distant cloud regions. Verizon first validated the idea by installing MongoDB Community at the edge of a Wavelength zone and measuring a 47% throughput improvement. The production design adds Atlas Functions to direct clients to the closest database instance through Verizon’s edge discovery service, while Atlas Device Sync and Realm keep data synchronized among devices, edge virtual machines, and the cloud without developers having to manage conflict resolution. The full architecture can be stood up in minutes across 19 AWS Wavelength zones and gives Verizon a platform for low-latency mobile, IoT, and machine-learning use cases at the network edge.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed database layer Verizon uses to persist and serve edge data across its 5G footprint.

solution_components.name: Atlas Device Sync
solution_components.role: Synchronizes data automatically between edge instances, the cloud, and connected devices without custom conflict-resolution logic.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Realm
solution_components.role: Extends data persistence and application logic to Verizon’s mobile edge compute footprint.

solution_components.name: Atlas Functions
solution_components.role: Works with Verizon’s edge discovery service to route mobile clients to the nearest database instance.

data_flow: Device and application data are routed to the nearest edge database instance, stored through Atlas and Realm in AWS Wavelength zones, synchronized with Atlas Device Sync across edge and cloud environments, and then analyzed or served back to mobile and IoT applications with lower latency.
business_outcome: Verizon gained a lower-latency edge data architecture that can improve user experiences, reduce networking costs, and accelerate new 5G applications that depend on synchronized operational data at the edge.
metrics: Verizon has over 140 million retail connections and is deploying across 19 AWS Wavelength zones.
The initial proof of concept showed a 47% improvement in throughput compared to the existing network path.
The reference architecture can be stood up in minutes across all 19 AWS Wavelength Zones.
architecture_clues: Atlas Functions integrate with Verizon’s edge discovery service to route clients to the closest database.
Atlas Device Sync hides conflict resolution for developers running across edge zones.
Realm instances run on virtual machines across AWS Wavelength zones.
The design supports mobile, IoT, and machine-learning workloads that keep data at the network edge.
